source.title: Reparameterized LLM Training via Orthogonal Equivalence Transformation
source.authors: Ze-Ju Qiu; Simon Buchholz; Tim Z. Xiao; M. Dax; Bernhard Scholkopf; Weiyang Liu

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own results that POET and other training methods differ in held-out validation performance and in measured weight-spectrum properties, refining the broad generalization claim for LLM pretraining. It does not test random-label memorization or the specific versioned conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper compares POET with AdamW, GaLore, LoRA, and other methods on validation perplexity, and measures singular spectra, hyperspherical energy, and vector-probing dynamics. These results concern held-out language-model performance and related properties, but do not test any listed claim version's specified behavior. Cited prior-work claims about generalization are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates POET's language-model performance and spectral properties, but none of V1–V8. Appendix E states that all training runs use AdamW: POET versus direct training therefore does not test V4's adaptive-versus-SGD comparison. Spectral entropy, spectral norms and hyperspherical energy do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or its correlation with generalization gaps. The record's tests/T5 classification is incorrect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors present POET as a spectrum-preserving, parameter-efficient reparameterization that improves validation perplexity and downstream performance. Their stronger assertion of improvement across every GLUE task and finetuning method is contradicted by the full-finetuning STS-B result, 0.873 versus 0.880.
record.recipe_differences: The paper introduces POET, a spectrum-preserving reparameterized training method; it compares against AdamW and other LLM training baselines. It does not use the versioned original methods or tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: Validation perplexity varies with model size, parameter budget, initialization scheme, merge-then-reinitialize frequency, and number of Neumann terms; vector-probing trajectories are reported across layers and projection types.

fits_no_version.finding: POET-FS b=1/2 achieves lower C4 validation perplexity than direct AdamW training at all five reported model scales, including 16.90 versus 19.61 at 3B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectrum-preserving reparameterization with POET can improve held-out language-model performance over direct AdamW training in the tested setups.

fits_no_version.finding: POET maintains spectral diversity, approximately preserves initialized singular values, maintains low hyperspherical energy and exhibits characteristic vector-probe dynamics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: POET constrains weight geometry during training; these measurements alone do not establish a sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation perplexity depends on initialization, merge/reinitialization frequency and Neumann approximation order; k=0 diverges.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: POET's performance and stability depend on its initialization and approximation configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: With full finetuning, POET pretraining improves seven of eight GLUE metrics; STS-B decreases from 0.880 to 0.873.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: POET pretraining improves most tested downstream GLUE scores, with task-dependent exceptions.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code will be released prior to publication
record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the tabulated comparisons. It does not evaluate train-test error gaps, random-label memorization, or any of the eight claim versions. Some qualitative curve comparisons are shown only in figures without exact values. The authors state that the exact mechanism behind POET's slower but stable progress remains an open question.
record.rows_left_out: None of the qualifying reported comparisons are left out; the listed claim versions are not tested. Table 4 has been recorded for all eight GLUE measures. No figure-only curve values were reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out performance and chance-level random-label held-out performance.
Width beyond the zero-training-error threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD/momentum optimization, tuning-dependent differences, optimizer switching and decoupled-weight-decay interventions.
Batch-size effects at fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps and comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All 33 rows fall outside V1–V8 and should not serve as evidence for those versions. POET is optimized with AdamW, so its advantage is not evidence that SGD generalizes better than adaptive optimizers. Additional OFT/POET GLUE finetuning comparisons and BART summarization results are omitted from the record, but they also test no listed version and therefore require no missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label classification comparison.
No width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison under the version's tuning conditions.
No large-batch versus small-batch comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout intervention or dropout/weight-decay comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison to norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples or retraining comparison.
